does: Drops spoonfuls of a thick mixture of grated vegetable, egg, cheese and a little flour into hot oil, flattens them lightly and turns them once, so that each fritter is crisp and golden outside and soft inside.
how: Make the mixture thick enough to sit on a spoon. If it runs, stir in a little more flour. If it is stiff and dry, loosen it with a spoonful of water.
Warm a shallow layer of oil in a wide pan until a crumb of the mixture sizzles at once.
Drop in spoonfuls with room between them, and press each to a flat round with the back of the spoon.
Leave them alone until the underside is deep golden and the edges look set, then turn each once.
Lift them onto a rack or paper to drain. Fry the rest in lots, and wipe the pan if bits of the mixture scorch.

cues.text: A steady, lively sizzle. A roar means the oil is too hot, and silence means it is too cool.
The edges turn lacy and golden before the middle sets.

mistakes.mistake: Frying in oil that is too cool, so that the fritters soak it up and turn greasy.
mistakes.fix: Wait for the sizzle before the first spoonful goes in.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding the pan, so that the fritters steam and join together.
mistakes.fix: Fry a few at a time, with room between them.

mistakes.mistake: Turning too soon, so that the fritter tears.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the underside is golden and the edges are set.

variant_of.differs: A fritter mixture has no shape of its own, so it is dropped in by the spoonful and flattened, in more oil than a cut of meat or fish would be fried in, and it is turned only once it has set.
